channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves Alphabet Changes, Adopting 28 Latin-Based Letters
item.description: The Uzbek Senate has approved amendments to the law on the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. The new alphabet will feature 28 letters and an apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three letter combinations. Documents and currency issued under the old alphabet will remain valid during the transition period.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits and Preferences for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A seminar in Surkhandarya discussed a presidential decree offering new benefits for entrepreneurs, including a three-year exemption from inspections for small businesses. The decree aims to reduce state interference and strengthen protections for businesses, fostering economic growth.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Discuss Cooperation Development in Minsk
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS member states met in Minsk to discuss cooperation. Delegations from Azerbaijan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, UAE, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on information exchange, existing problems, and solutions for enhancing regional law enforcement collaboration.

item.title: Putin: Migration processes generated 321 billion rubles for Russian budget
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that migration processes generated 321 billion rubles in revenue for the state over the past 1.5 years. Over 60 billion rubles went to the federal budget, and over 250-260 billion to regional budgets. Around 100,000 migrants who committed violations were expelled from Russia.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes land transfer for foreign property buyers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a new law requiring foreigners to transfer land ownership to the state when purchasing real estate. The land would be leased back for up to 50 years. This proposal aims to regulate foreign ownership of land associated with properties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan presents investment potential at China International Fair
item.description: Kyrgyzstan showcased its investment potential at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen. The event provided a platform to present investment opportunities, attract capital, and foster collaboration with international businesses and investors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Criminal Liability for Illegal Underground Tunnels
item.description: Uzbekistan is establishing criminal liability for the construction and use of illegal underground tunnels across its state border. The Senate approved amendments to the Criminal and Criminal Procedure Codes. Senator Qutbiddin Burxonov stated that 12 such tunnels were discovered between 2016-2025, used to smuggle goods worth over $3.7 million and 5 kg of gold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Welcomed 9.1 Million Tourists in First Eight Months of 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan hosted 9.1 million foreign tourists from January to August 2026, a 21.1% increase compared to the same period in 2025. August alone saw nearly 1.5 million visitors. Tourism revenue from services reached $4.6 billion, up 53.5% year-on-year. Significant growth was noted from Asian, US, Russian, and European countries.

item.title: Seven Percent of Kyrgyzstanis Lost Money Due to Cyberattacks, Survey Finds
item.description: A 2025 Financial Literacy Survey by the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan reveals that seven percent of surveyed citizens lost money due to hacking or phishing attacks, up from four percent in 2021. The proportion of respondents who experienced bank card detail theft rose to three percent. Digital financial literacy remains a concern, with 30% unsure how to handle suspicious messages.

item.title: Glaciers in Tajikistan's GBAO Show 1.5-2 Meter Decrease in Level
item.description: An international research expedition in August 2026 on glaciers in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) recorded a 1.5-2 meter drop in ice levels. The study, involving Tajik scientists and Swiss university representatives, aims to assess glacier dynamics and their role in water resource regulation amid climate change.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to establish international transport and logistics center in Sary-Tash
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Investment Agency and Textile Trans LLC signed a memorandum to create the Sary-Tash international transport and logistics center. The project aims to attract $100 million in investment and enhance Kyrgyzstan's role as a trade hub between China, Central Asia, and South Asia.

item.title: Bishkek City Court deliberates on "Letter of 75" case verdict
item.description: The Bishkek City Court has retired to chambers to issue a verdict in the "Letter of 75" case. Previously, the district court sentenced several former officials, including the ex-head of GKNB, to four years with probation. Both prosecution and defense appealed this sentence.

item.title: Bishkek to allow private cars on public transport lanes at night and weekends
item.description: Bishkek has approved new rules for dedicated public transport lanes. Private vehicles will be prohibited from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. At night and on weekends, private cars will be allowed to use these lanes. The municipality plans to install new signs and increase enforcement.

item.title: Ombudsman visits prisons, reports inmates have access to medical treatment
item.description: The Ombudsman visited prisons and reported that inmates have access to medical treatment. Ruhshona Hakimbova is learning English, but it remains unclear why the request for surgery for Pirmuhammadzoda's relatives was denied. The article mentions Pirmuhammadzoda is a journalist.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses inclusive education challenges and teacher preparedness
item.description: Uzbekistan is discussing challenges in inclusive education, with over 132,000 school-aged children with disabilities. Currently, 6,801 children are included in inclusive education, while 17,056 receive home-based education. Experts debated the pace versus quality of reforms and teacher readiness.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Discuss International Cooperation and Information Exchange
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS countries met in Minsk on September 9, 2026. Participants discussed international cooperation among internal affairs ministries and the development of information exchange via Interpol channels. They also reviewed participation in Interpol events aimed at improving the organization's charter and rules.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Head of Tashkent International Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, has been appointed as the manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center on a concurrent basis. This new role adds to her existing responsibilities within the presidential administration.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Keyboard Layout for New Alphabet Letters
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to adapt state information systems to a new alphabet, including letters Ö, Ğ, Ş, and Ç. The Ministry of Digital Technologies is developing a unified technical standard for implementation. Data migration, search, and document circulation systems will be updated to accommodate the new characters.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Manager of Tashkent International Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, has been appointed manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center. She will also coordinate the center's activities, represent it internationally, and participate in personnel decisions. The center, established by presidential decree, will feature special legal and currency regimes.

item.title: UN Expert Calls for Protection of Elderly Rights Regardless of Age or Diagnosis
item.description: An independent UN expert urges a new approach to protecting the rights of the elderly, emphasizing that cognitive impairments do not diminish human dignity or fundamental rights. He warns against ageism and decisions made for the elderly without considering their will, highlighting the difference between brain changes and loss of personhood.

item.title: Criminal Liability to Be Established for Illegal Tunnels at Uzbekistan's Border
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish separate criminal liability for constructing illegal tunnels across its border. It was found that 12 illegal underground structures and tunnels were built over 10 years. A law approved by the Senate will impose stricter penalties for those using them to cross the border or smuggle goods.

item.title: Family Restoring Bukhara's Sarrofon Bathhouse May Lose Management Rights
item.description: A family that has restored and maintained the 16th-century Sarrofon Bathhouse in Bukhara for nearly 30 years faces potential loss of management rights. After the investor's death in 2019, the building was listed as a cultural heritage site, and a legal dispute arose over its lease.

item.title: Tajikistan Strengthens Counter-Terrorism Cooperation Amidst Globalization Challenges
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Interior Minister attended international events in China focusing on combating terrorism, extremism, and transnational crime. The conference emphasized the global nature of these threats and the need for enhanced international cooperation. Participants discussed new security challenges and the importance of digital methods for crime prevention and counteraction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Defendant in Power Seizure Case Requests Open Trial from President
item.description: Temirlan Sultanbekov, on trial for an alleged attempt to seize power, has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for a public trial. Having spent significant time in detention, he argues an open trial would demonstrate the fairness of the investigation and judicial process. He states he seeks nothing for himself, only justice.

item.title: Over 96,000 Uzbek Citizens Returned from Russia in 10 Days
item.description: More than 96,000 Uzbek citizens have returned to Uzbekistan from Russia in the past 10 days. Over 54,000 came directly from Russia, while the rest transited through Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to citizens facing difficult situations.

item.title: All Uzbek school textbooks to transition to new alphabet by 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to fully transition all school textbooks to the updated Uzbek alphabet between 2027 and 2031. The Deputy Minister of Preschool and School Education stated that textbooks for first graders will use the new alphabet starting in 2027, with all textbooks updated by 2031.

item.title: Five arrested at Namangan airport attempting to smuggle gold worth $1.1 billion to India
item.description: Five individuals were apprehended at Namangan International Airport for attempting to illegally export gold worth 1.1 billion soums to India. The suspects, from Andijan and Fergana regions, were using their bodies as 'live containers' to smuggle 555 grams of gold bars and 200 grams of jewelry.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves New 28-Letter Latin-Based Alphabet Variant
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan approved a new variant of the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet, consisting of 28 letters and one apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three digraphs. The proposed reform aims to align the writing system with the "one sound - one letter" principle and address issues with digital usage. The bill now moves to the president for review.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Showcases First Robotic Surgery System at Medical Academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's first robotic surgery system was unveiled at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. The Ministry of Health reported that the robot assists surgeons by enabling precise instrument control and magnified views through small incisions, enhancing complex operations.

item.title: UzAuto Motors Launches First Chevrolet Hybrid Model, the Equinox PHEV
item.description: UzAuto Motors has announced the launch of its first hybrid model, the Chevrolet Equinox PHEV crossover. Available in two trims, the vehicle features a plug-in hybrid system allowing short trips on electric power alone, with a total range exceeding 1000 km.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election Date Set for January 27, 2027, Parliament to Confirm
item.description: The Zhogorku Kenesh (parliament) is expected to officially set the presidential election date for January 27, 2027, on September 24. The Central Election Commission stated that the election will proceed on this date regardless of parliamentary resolution, with campaigning to begin in December.

item.title: Uzbekistan Privatizes State Assets Worth Over $8 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's president has approved a large-scale privatization program, offering state assets valued at approximately $8 billion for public auction. The program includes stakes in 84 companies, over 1,200 real estate objects, and about 8,000 hectares of land. The goal is to raise at least $1.17 billion by the end of 2026.

item.title: GKNB uncovers state damage in purchase of two combine harvesters in Naryn region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has identified state damage amounting to 4.945 million soms during the procurement of two combine harvesters in the Min-Bulak rural district of Naryn region. Criminal proceedings are underway to investigate the actions of involved officials and recover the losses.

item.title: Imprisoned politician Temirlan Sultanbekov writes letter to Kyrgyzstan's president
item.description: Imprisoned politician Temirlan Sultanbekov has written a letter to President Sadyr Japarov from pre-trial detention center SIZO-1. Sultanbekov stated he would not ask for mercy, emphasizing his commitment to the 'Kyrgyz spirit,' and requested an open trial.

item.title: Russian scientists to study infections in Kyrgyzstan with population surveys
item.description: The St. Petersburg Pasteur Research Institute will organize population studies in Kyrgyzstan from October 16 to November 15, 2026. The research aims to study infections, involving the collection and laboratory testing of biological samples from 70 points across the country.

item.title: Sughd region plans to process waste into organic fertilizers
item.description: Officials in Tajikistan's Sughd region met with Iranian counterparts to discuss cooperation in waste management and recycling. Plans include updating sewage networks, reconstructing landfills, and implementing technologies to produce organic fertilizers from waste, potentially starting in Khujand.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Housing Market Sees 21% Growth in Seven Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's housing market experienced a 21% increase in sales during the first seven months of the year. The number of real estate transactions rose to 34,300. Sales growth was observed in most regions, with the highest figures recorded in the capital city.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan introduces first robotic surgical system at medical academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Medical Academy has unveiled the country's first robotic surgical system. The system enhances surgeon precision and visualization through small incisions, but the doctor remains in full control during operations. The academy plans to begin robot-assisted surgeries soon, with another system to be acquired for the National Center for Mother and Child Healthcare.

item.title: Two former police officers in Syrdarya sentenced to 5 and 6 years for bribery
item.description: Two former officers from the Khovos district police department in Syrdarya region were sentenced to five and six years in prison for demanding bribes. They were accused of fabricating evidence and extorting money from a farmer regarding a land dispute. The officers were apprehended while receiving part of the demanded sum.

item.title: Uzbek citizens returning from abroad can receive grants up to 60 million soums for business expansion
item.description: Uzbek citizens who worked abroad and returned to start businesses can receive grants up to 60 million soums to expand their ventures and create jobs. The program, a collaboration between the Migration Agency and IOM with Swedish funding, targets returnees from 2025-2026. Special support is given to women entrepreneurs.
